SdFat already defines FAT_TYPE_FAT12=12, FAT_TYPE_FAT16=16, FAT_TYPE_FAT32=32 (.pio/libdeps/cyd/SdFat/src/FatLib/FatPartition.h) and FAT_TYPE_EXFAT=64 (.pio/libdeps/cyd/SdFat/src/ExFatLib/ExFatPartition.h).

The sibling function cardTypeName() in src/hardware/sd_card.cpp already switches on SdFat's named SD_CARD_TYPE_SD1/SD2/SDHC constants for the analogous card-type classification, so the named-constant convention exists in the same file family but was not applied consistently to fsName().

issues.summary: One lone static_cast in card_format.cpp against otherwise universal C-style casts looks like an abandoned safety-cast migration
issues.suggestion: Pick one cast convention and apply it uniformly: either convert the remaining C-style numeric/pointer casts to static_cast (or reinterpret_cast where a pointer's underlying type genuinely changes, e.g. the heap_caps_malloc void* casts), or revert the single static_cast in card_format.cpp to match the codebase's established C-style convention -- do not leave one file as the sole outlier.
evidence: src/util/card_format.cpp:60 is the codebase's only static_cast: static_cast<unsigned long>(hz / 1000UL).

Every other numeric or pointer conversion in the codebase uses a C-style cast instead, e.g. sd_card.cpp:235 (uint8_t*)heap_caps_malloc(...), touch_calibration.cpp:40/49 (int)mapRange(...), benchmark.cpp:67/141/210, benchmark_raw.cpp:15/32/96/113, display_results.cpp:256/274, bench_math.cpp:51, ui_geometry.cpp:27.

add.header: Strictly layered, acyclic module graph
add.description: coupling_matrix across core/util/hardware/ui/benchmark shows only downward edges (util->core, hardware->core/util, ui->hardware/core, benchmark->core/hardware/ui) with no reverse edges and no cycles anywhere in the 31-file tree.

add.header: core/ headers are inert data, not behavioral hubs
add.description: config.h (10 importers) and app_types.h (8 importers) top the god_modules signal by importer count, but both are pure constexpr constants and plain structs/enums with near-zero fan-out and no logic, so their high fan-in doesn't create the blast-radius risk a behavioral hub would.

add.header: Consistent public/internal header split in ui/ and benchmark/
add.description: Both src/ui (display_ui.h + display_ui_internal.h) and src/benchmark (benchmark.h + benchmark_internal.h) use the same convention: a small public API header plus an explicitly-commented 'not part of the public API' internal header shared by several .cpp implementation files. The pattern repeats across directories instead of being one-off.

add.header: benchmark.cpp's UI coupling is documented and invariant-driven
add.description: benchmark.cpp calls uiShowProgress() directly during its I/O loops, which is the only non-downward edge in the dependency graph. CLAUDE.md documents this as load-bearing: timing measurement brackets only the SD I/O call, with UI updates explicitly placed outside the timed interval to keep reported MB/s accurate. The sibling spi_scale_benchmark.cpp (same directory, same kind of I/O loop) has zero UI dependency, showing the coupling is an intentional per-case UX choice, not an accidental leak.

add.header: Host-testable vs hardware-coupled split matches architecture docs
add.description: test/ covers exactly the modules whose headers are commented as hardware-independent (bench_math, ui_geometry, card_format, card_identity, touch_calibration, app_types), while hardware/UI-dependent modules (sd_card, touch, display_ui, benchmark orchestration) are correctly left to on-device validation only. Runtime structure matches the documented architecture in CLAUDE.md almost exactly.

add.header: Domain-aligned top-level package split
add.description: src/ divides into core/ (shared constants and data types), hardware/ (SD and touch drivers), benchmark/ (performance measurement), ui/ (TFT rendering and hit-testing), and util/ (pure formatting/identity/calibration helpers) — each directory maps to one domain capability rather than an accidental grouping, and a new engineer can predict where new code of a given kind belongs.

add.header: CLAUDE.md architecture narrative verified accurate
add.description: CLAUDE.md's per-module descriptions (sd_card.* scope, diagnostics.* as thin glue, v0.7 dead-code removal) were checked against the actual source and held up exactly — including confirming via grep that documented removed dead-code (SHARED_SPI, lastTitle, chunk-sweep knobs) is genuinely absent from src/. This makes the project's docs a trustworthy map rather than aspirational text.

add.header: Consistent pure-logic/host-testable extraction pattern
add.description: bench_math.h, ui_geometry.h, card_format.h, card_identity.h, and touch_calibration.h each carry the identical 'Pure ... no hardware/Arduino dependency, safe to unit-test on host' comment and each has a matching test/test_X directory. This is the same architectural decision applied independently across every subsystem (benchmark, ui, hardware support, util), rather than a one-off.

add.header: Public facade + internal header pattern reused across subsystems
add.description: Both benchmark/ and ui/ follow the same shape: one public header (benchmark.h / display_ui.h) plus one internal-only header (benchmark_internal.h / display_ui_internal.h) shared across multiple .cpp files in that directory. Grep confirms each internal header is only included from within its own directory — the internal/public boundary is never crossed.

add.header: config.h and app_types.h are legitimate high-fan-in cores, not dumping grounds
add.description: The mechanical scan flags config.h (10 importers) and app_types.h (8 importers) as god modules, but their content is exclusively pin/timing/size constants and shared POD struct/enum definitions respectively, matching their stated single-purpose roles. High fan-in here reflects genuine foundational status, not concern mixing.

add.header: Uniform naming across all directories
add.description: camelCase functions, PascalCase types, and SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE constants are applied without exception across benchmark/, hardware/, ui/, util/, and core/, so a developer can predict casing without checking a style guide.

add.header: Consistent static-linkage idiom for private helpers
add.description: 7 of 8 files with file-local helper functions use `static` for internal linkage (sd_card.cpp, benchmark.cpp, display_ui.cpp, display_results.cpp, main.cpp, plus header-only files); this is the codebase's established idiom against which touch_calibration.cpp's anonymous-namespace usage is an outlier.

add.header: Shared *_internal.h pattern for non-public internals
add.description: benchmark_internal.h and display_ui_internal.h both use the same documented pattern (a header explicitly marked 'not part of the public X.h API') for internals shared across more than one .cpp in the same directory, applied consistently in two different subsystems.

add.header: Split-declaration/multi-implementation pattern is intentional, not inconsistent
add.description: benchmark.h's two functions are implemented in separate benchmark.cpp/spi_scale_benchmark.cpp files, and display_ui.h's functions are split across display_ui.cpp/display_diagnostics.cpp/display_progress.cpp/display_results.cpp by screen concern. This is the same deliberate pattern used in two directories (group public declarations in one header, split implementations by cohesive sub-concern), not an inconsistency to unify.

add.header: Dominant vertical one-argument-per-line formatting style
add.description: The large majority of files (benchmark/*, ui/*, util/card_format.cpp, util/touch_calibration.cpp, hardware/sd_card.cpp bodies, main.cpp) wrap multi-argument calls and declarations one argument per line; this is the baseline convention against which hardware/touch.* is a visible style island.

add.header: Uniform bool + result-struct error strategy
add.description: Every I/O-facing function in src/ (scanCard, timedFileWrite/Read, verifyFile, rawReadAtCurrentSpeed, runSpiScalingBenchmark) returns bool and reports failure detail through an output struct field rather than exceptions or sentinel values, so a developer can predict the failure shape of any new function before reading its body.

add.header: Rich SD error-code capture at hardware boundary
add.description: sd.sdErrorCode()/sd.sdErrorData() are captured into AttemptResult/SpiScalePoint on every card-level failure (init/CID/CSD/read) in both sd_card.cpp and spi_scale_benchmark.cpp, and rendered on the diagnostics screen -- giving the same diagnostic depth to failures raised from two different modules.

add.header: No exception usage anywhere in src/
add.description: Consistent with an Arduino/ESP32 embedded target, the codebase never mixes exceptions with bool/struct error reporting -- there is exactly one error-propagation vocabulary in use throughout src/.

add.header: volumeBegin() failure lacks error-code capture
add.description: Unlike card init/CID/CSD/read failures, a failed sd.volumeBegin() in scanCard() only flips info.volumeOk to false with no sdErrorCode()/sdErrorData() captured, leaving 'not mounted' failures less diagnosable than every sibling failure mode.

add.header: Strict ui-prefixed verb+noun convention for display API
add.description: Every public function in src/ui/display_ui.h follows ui<Verb><Noun> (uiShowX/uiDrawX/uiHitTestX/uiWaitForTap), letting callers in main.cpp predict module and behavior from the name alone. Consistent across every screen file (display_progress.cpp, display_results.cpp, display_diagnostics.cpp).

add.header: Units and outcome encoded directly in field/function names
add.description: Struct fields and return values consistently bake in units and success semantics (fileWriteMBs, activeSpiHz, filesystemDataBytes, preallocMs, efficiencyPercent, *Ok booleans in AttemptResult/CardInfo/BenchmarkResult), removing ambiguity about scale or type without needing to check implementations.

add.header: No generic/vague verbs found in production code
add.description: Across all 31 src/ files (~3100 LOC), no function uses process/handle/do/manage-style generic naming; even small helpers (resolveVendor, repeatedBufferCrc32, spiEfficiencyPercent) name their exact computation.

add.header: showDiagnosticsScreen vs uiShowDiagnostics naming collision
add.description: The only diagnostics-screen orchestrator bundles draw+wait under a name nearly identical to the draw-only uiShowDiagnostics(), breaking the otherwise consistent pattern where main.cpp explicitly pairs show+wait for every other screen.

add.header: Pure-logic modules split out for host-side unit testing
add.description: bench_math, card_format, card_identity, touch_calibration, and ui_geometry are deliberately isolated from Arduino/TFT_eSPI/SdFat dependencies specifically so they can be unit-tested on the host (each header says so explicitly), which is the reason these modules exist as separate translation units rather than being inlined into their hardware-facing callers.

add.header: No OOP/DI ceremony; free functions over module-static state
add.description: The codebase has no classes, interfaces, or generics anywhere in src/; every module is a set of free functions closing over file-static state (e.g. sd_card.cpp's static SdFs sd, display_ui_internal.cpp's function-local static TFT_eSPI). This is proportionate for a 31-file embedded diagnostic tool and avoids abstraction layers the domain doesn't need.

add.header: internal.h headers carry real shared logic, not facades
add.description: benchmark_internal.h (allocateDmaBuffer, rawReadAtCurrentSpeed) and display_ui_internal.h (tft(), header(), lineRow()) are genuine shared-internals headers consumed by multiple sibling .cpp files with real logic behind them, not re-export facades.

add.header: sd_card.h deliberately exposes a raw SdFat escape hatch
add.description: getSd() intentionally returns the raw SdFs so the two benchmark call sites that need raw sector/file I/O can use it directly, instead of sd_card.h growing a redundant wrapper API over SdFat's own methods. The cardTypeName() comment shows this module boundary was drawn deliberately rather than by accident.

add.header: Inconsistent extraction granularity for one-off orchestration glue
add.description: showDiagnosticsScreen() (src/ui/diagnostics.cpp) is functionally the same kind of thin, single-caller orchestration as rescan() and runBenchMenu() in main.cpp, but only it was given its own header/cpp pair — the codebase has no settled rule for when glue code becomes its own module.

add.header: Minimal, purpose-built dependency footprint
add.description: Only two runtime libraries exist (TFT_eSPI for display, SdFat for the SD/filesystem layer), each used broadly and proportionately across the src tree with no overlapping/duplicate-purpose library and no unused dependency.

add.header: Touch driver avoids an extra library
add.description: src/hardware/touch.cpp bit-bangs the XPT2046-style SPI protocol directly instead of adding a touch-controller library, keeping the dependency count low for a feature that is simple enough to implement inline.

add.header: lib_deps entries are unpinned
add.description: platformio.ini declares TFT_eSPI and SdFat with no version constraint, so PlatformIO resolves to the latest published release on a clean environment/CI build rather than a known-good version, which is a real risk given TFT_eSPI's history of breaking build-flag config changes across releases.

add.header: Pure math/formatting helpers are small and precise
add.description: bench_math.cpp, card_format.cpp, card_identity.cpp, touch_calibration.cpp, and ui_geometry.cpp are consistently small, single-purpose, side-effect-free functions with exact edge-case handling (clamping, rounding thresholds) — this is the strongest corner of the codebase from a low-level-elegance perspective.

add.header: Staged SPI qualification loop uses direct guard-clause continues
add.description: sd_card.cpp's scanCard() steps through SPI speeds with early `continue` on each failure stage (init/CID/CSD/read) rather than nested conditionals, keeping the happy path visible despite four sequential failure points.

add.header: Two incompatible statement-formatting styles coexist
add.description: Roughly half the .cpp files (benchmark/, most of ui/, hardware/sd_card.cpp) fragment nearly every statement across multiple lines, while the other half (util/, bench_math.cpp, ui_geometry.cpp, touch.cpp, display_ui_internal.cpp) use conventional compact formatting for equivalent code, making local readability unpredictable across the tree.

add.header: Benchmark chunked I/O loops are triplicated
add.description: timedFileWrite, timedFileRead, and verifyFile in benchmark.cpp reimplement the same chunking/timing/progress-reporting loop three times with only the inner I/O call differing.

add.header: Struct DTOs form explicit boundary contracts
add.description: CardInfo, AttemptResult, BenchmarkResult, and SpiScaleResult in core/app_types.h are essentially the only data that crosses hardware/benchmark/ui boundaries; they are passed by value or const reference with no ad-hoc mapper layer, so each seam's inputs/outputs are explicit and minimal.

add.header: main.cpp reads as pure composition
add.description: setup()/loop()/rescan()/runBenchMenu() in main.cpp just sequence calls to initTouch/initSdHardware/scanCard/getCardInfo/ui* functions with no business logic of their own, so a new developer can trace the whole app's control flow from this one file without tangled back-and-forth.

add.header: Pure-logic modules declare their testable boundary explicitly
add.description: bench_math.h, card_format.h, card_identity.h, ui_geometry.h, and touch_calibration.h each carry a header comment stating they have no hardware/Arduino dependency and are unit-tested on host, giving each hardware/logic seam a clearly stated contract rather than leaving it implicit.

add.header: Benchmark loops call UI progress functions directly
add.description: timedFileWrite/timedFileRead/verifyFile in benchmark.cpp call uiShowProgress() directly from inside their I/O loops rather than through a callback/observer abstraction. This crosses the benchmark->ui boundary directly, but is applied consistently everywhere progress is reported and avoids indirection ceremony that wouldn't pay for itself in this single-threaded firmware.

add.header: Pure-logic modules have thorough boundary-focused unit tests
add.description: bench_math, card_format, card_identity, touch_calibration, ui_geometry, and app_types are each covered by a host-native Unity suite that asserts on boundary values (GiB/MiB cutoff, clamping, out-of-range clamping, zero-division guards) and documents non-obvious default-value invariants (e.g. BenchmarkResult::cleanupOk defaulting true) rather than just happy-path values.

add.header: No snapshot tests and no test-production coupling
add.description: Every test asserts a specific computed value or string against the module's declared public header API; none reach into internals or rely on golden-file/snapshot comparison, so the suite is naturally resistant to implementation-detail churn.

add.header: Hardware-coupled critical paths are untested by structural necessity
add.description: scanCard()'s SPI qualification sequencing, benchmark.cpp's write/read/verify guard chain, the SPI scaling loop, and touch's bit-banged SPI reads have zero coverage, but no mock Arduino/SdFat/TFT_eSPI layer exists in the project, making this accepted debt rather than a strategy failure; the guard-clause style in these files is direct enough to partially offset the risk.

add.header: CLAUDE.md misstates that no test suite exists
add.description: The project's own architecture doc tells a developer to validate purely by flashing hardware, actively hiding the existence of the env:native Unity suite defined in platformio.ini — a documentation/reality mismatch specific to how a developer discovers and trusts the test strategy.

add.header: Consistent inputs-before-outputs parameter ordering
add.description: Every function using reference/pointer out-parameters (readTouch, mapTouchToScreen, timedFileWrite/Read, verifyFile, rawReadAtCurrentSpeed) places inputs first and outputs last, so a developer can predict parameter order from any single example.

add.header: Uniform uiShow*/uiDraw*/uiHitTest* family shape
add.description: All display_ui.h entry points take the relevant domain struct by const reference and return void or a plain action enum, with no mixed styles across the family.

add.header: Edge-case return behavior documented on pure helpers
add.description: bench_math.h and ui_geometry.h document what a function returns at boundary inputs (e.g. hz==0, maxValue<=0) directly in header comments, giving callers an explicit contract without exceptions or Optional types.

add.header: scanCard vs runSpiScalingBenchmark result-shape asymmetry
add.description: Two structurally identical multi-speed SPI probing operations expose per-attempt error detail differently: scanCard() via global getters (getAttempts/getAttemptCount), runSpiScalingBenchmark() via a directly returned struct. See issue sd_scan_result_shape_asymmetry.

add.header: No authorization surface exists or is needed
add.description: CYD SD Tester is single-user ESP32 firmware controlling a local touchscreen and SD card slot; it has no network listeners, accounts, routes, or privilege tiers. A repo-wide scan for auth/permission/credential/role/admin terms found only an unrelated comment about SD-card vendor-ID heuristics. The dimension's look_for patterns (auth decorators on some routes, RLS gaps, permission-string literals, admin bypass) have no applicable surface in this codebase, so this is correctly scored high rather th

add.header: Header comments explain WHY, not WHAT
add.description: Comments in bench_math.h, ui_geometry.h, card_identity.h, touch_calibration.h, and sd_card.h consistently document non-obvious rationale (host-testability boundaries, the touch panel's X/Y axis swap, the SDHC/SDXC capacity threshold) rather than restating the adjacent code, and trivial functions carry no comments at all.

add.header: Domain-specific naming, no generic handlers
add.description: Function names across the codebase (crc32Update, spiEfficiencyPercent, cardTypeName, resolveVendor, identityCheckName) are precise and domain-aligned; no handleData/processItem/doOperation-style generic names were found.

add.header: Uniform one-item-per-line call formatting
add.description: Nearly every function call and multi-part expression across all 31 files is broken one argument/operand per line, even trivial single-token returns (e.g. `return\n HomeAction::Rescan;`). This is applied with total consistency codebase-wide, so per system-prompt guidance on uniform style choices it is recorded as a neutral characteristic rather than a defect, though it substantially inflates file length.

add.header: v0.7 dead-code removal verified complete in source
add.description: README.md/CLAUDE.md document specific removals (raw chunk sweep, best-chunk fields, SHARED_SPI A/B toggle, yield toggles, raw-progress toggle, hidden lastTitle state, old filesystemBytes naming, separate BENCH/SCALE buttons) from v0.7; grepping src/ for each of these symbols returns zero hits, confirming the documentation matches runtime reality rather than being aspirational.

add.header: No compile-time or runtime toggles for retired strategies
add.description: platformio.ini's USE_SPI_ARRAY_TRANSFER=1 and sd_card.cpp's DEDICATED_SPI are single fixed values with no alternate path defined anywhere, so there is no dual old/new SPI strategy left coexisting in the build.

add.header: Intentional SPI speed-ladder asymmetry, not migration drift
add.description: SPI_SPEEDS (normal scan, excludes 40MHz) vs SPI_SCALE_SPEEDS (diagnostic, includes 40MHz) looks like an inconsistency but is explicitly documented in CLAUDE.md as a deliberate, permanent decision -- correctly out of scope for incomplete_migration per the dimension's skip list.

add.header: Domain-based reorg into core/hardware/benchmark/ui/util
add.description: The former flat src/ layout was split into five domain folders with an acyclic dependency graph: core/ (config + shared types, fan_in 9.0) sits under everything, hardware/ and util/ sit above core/, and ui/ and benchmark/ sit above hardware/. No reciprocal directory edges exist in the coupling matrix, so a developer can reason about change blast-radius from directory alone.

add.header: core/ is a legitimate high-fan-in shared layer
add.description: src/core/config.h and src/core/app_types.h are imported across every other subdirectory (benchmark, hardware, ui, util) and by multiple test targets -- exactly the 'genuinely core' profile the package_organization rubric exempts from stragglerhood.

add.header: ui/ file count is justified by screen-based cohesion
add.description: ui/ has 11 files, above the flat-overload count threshold, but each file owns a distinct, non-overlapping concern (home screen, diagnostics screen + controller, progress screen, results screen, shared drawing primitives, pure geometry math) rather than mixing unrelated responsibilities, so it does not read as a dumping ground despite the count.

add.header: util/ directory's extraction rule is applied inconsistently
add.description: util/ was created to hold pure, hardware-independent, host-testable logic, but only 3 of the 5 modules matching that description (card_format, card_identity, touch_calibration) were moved there; bench_math and ui_geometry carry the identical rationale comment yet remain inside benchmark/ and ui/. This means the util/ boundary does not reliably predict where pure logic lives -- see the util_dir_hardware_affinity_mismatch issue.

add.header: Boot sequence centralized in main.cpp setup()
add.description: initDisplay(), initTouch(), initSdHardware(), then rescan() run in one explicit, linear block in setup() — there is exactly one place a developer needs to look to understand hardware bring-up order, and no module depends on being imported/linked in a particular order.

add.header: TFT singleton is a lazy Meyers singleton
add.description: display_ui_internal.cpp's tft() returns a function-local static TFT_eSPI instance, constructed on first call rather than at global static-init time, which eliminates any static-initialization-order risk between translation units.

add.header: Hardware singletons only reachable via accessor functions
add.description: sd, sdSPI, info, attempts, cid, csd in sd_card.cpp are file-scope statics never exposed as externs; every consumer goes through getSd()/getCardInfo()/getAttempts(), keeping the coupling explicit and centralized in sd_card.h's contract.

add.header: SD singleton restore relies on convention, not enforcement
add.description: runSpiScalingBenchmark() mutates the shared SdFs state across several SPI speeds and depends on its own trailing scanCard() call (explained only by a comment) to restore normal qualified state; nothing in the type system or call structure would catch a future edit that dropped or reordered that restore step.

add.header: UI screens built from small reusable draw primitives
add.description: header(), lineRow(), drawButton(), and drawHorizontalBar() are shared internal primitives (display_ui_internal.cpp) that every uiShow*/uiDraw* function composes from, keeping each screen function focused on layout instead of reimplementing text/color/rect boilerplate.

add.header: Domain state grouped into purpose-built structs
add.description: CardInfo, BenchmarkResult, SpiScaleResult/SpiScalePoint, and AttemptResult (src/core/app_types.h) group related fields by domain meaning, so functions take few, semantically coherent parameters instead of long unrelated parameter lists.

add.header: Pure math/format helpers are hardware-independent and narrowly scoped
add.description: bench_math.cpp, ui_geometry.cpp, card_format.cpp, and card_identity.cpp each expose small, single-purpose functions with no Arduino/TFT/SdFat dependency, making them directly unit-testable (test/test_bench_math, test/test_ui_geometry) and easy to reason about in isolation.

add.header: Report-printing split is inconsistent between sd_card and benchmark
add.description: sd_card.cpp separates its Serial report into printCardIdentity(), but benchmark.cpp's runQuickBenchmark() inlines an equivalent report block instead of following that established split, and the three benchmark loop functions duplicate the same chunked-progress scaffold.

add.header: Pure-function docstrings match implementation exactly
add.description: bench_math.h, card_format.h, card_identity.h, ui_geometry.h, and touch_calibration.h document edge-case behavior (e.g. computeBarFillWidth's 'returns 0 if maxValue <= 0') and the corresponding .cpp files implement exactly what is documented, with no drift found.

add.header: get-prefixed accessors are all side-effect-free
add.description: getSd(), getCardInfo(), getAttempts(), and getAttemptCount() in sd_card.h/.cpp are pure reads of module-static state; none of them mutate on read, honoring the 'getX' naming contract consistently across the hardware module.

add.header: uiHitTest* functions are pure predicates
add.description: uiHitTestHome and uiHitTestBenchMenu only test coordinates against button rectangles and return an action enum; they never draw or mutate UI/global state, unlike the uiDraw*/uiShow* functions they pair with.

add.header: runSpiScalingBenchmark has an undisclosed rescan side effect
add.description: Unlike its sibling runQuickBenchmark, runSpiScalingBenchmark triggers a full scanCard() re-qualification (mutating global CardInfo/AttemptResult state) both on early failure and at normal completion; this is explained only in a .cpp-local comment, not in the shared benchmark.h header both functions are declared in.

add.header: Uniform guard-clause ladder in SD scan/benchmark loops
add.description: scanCard(), timedFileWrite/Read, verifyFile, and rawReadAtCurrentSpeed all use the same 'check failure -> record error -> continue/return false' shape, keeping the happy path visually distinct from error handling across every I/O loop in the codebase.

add.header: Chained success guards prevent stale benchmark state
add.description: runQuickBenchmark() gates each dependent step (write -> read -> verify) behind '&& seekOk'/'&& prevStepOk' checks, so a failed earlier step correctly leaves later BenchmarkResult flags at their false default instead of running on inconsistent state.

add.header: Pure math/geometry helpers are unit-tested at their edges
add.description: bench_math.cpp and ui_geometry.cpp are hardware-independent by design and covered by test/test_bench_math and test/test_ui_geometry, which assert exact behavior at zero-time, zero-max, and partial-chunk edge cases — giving the control flow provable correctness rather than apparent correctness.

add.header: cardOk/cidOk/csdOk are a true design invariant, not redundant flags
add.description: These CardInfo booleans are only ever set together in fillCardIdentity(), reached solely after CID+CSD+sector-read all succeed in scanCard(); downstream 'if (info.cidOk)' checks are meaningful two-state guards rather than checks on a value that can't actually vary.

add.header: Enum classes used consistently and exhaustively
add.description: AttemptStage, HomeAction, and BenchMenuAction are all enum class, and every consumer (main.cpp's switch over HomeAction, display_ui.cpp's uiHitTestHome/uiHitTestBenchMenu, card_identity.cpp's attemptStageName) handles them exhaustively without falling back to raw int/string comparisons.

add.header: Domain data modeled as typed structs, not dynamic bags
add.description: CardInfo, AttemptResult, BenchmarkResult, and SpiScalePoint/SpiScaleResult in src/core/app_types.h are plain structs with explicit field types and default member initializers, so there is no dict[str, Any]-equivalent hiding the real shape of this data anywhere in the codebase.

add.header: Nullable buffer-allocation contract is honestly checked everywhere
add.description: allocateDmaBuffer() returns a nullable uint8_t*, and every call site in benchmark.cpp and spi_scale_benchmark.cpp checks the result before use, so the nullable return type is trustworthy in practice rather than being an unchecked Optional.

add.header: Raw uint8_t error/type codes mirror the external SdFat API boundary
add.description: CardInfo/AttemptResult expose raw uint8_t error and card/filesystem type codes because they come directly from SdFat's own raw-integer APIs (sd.sdErrorCode(), sd.card()->type(), sd.fatType()); this is a deliberate boundary decision forced by the external library, not a bypass of an in-house enum.
